implementationFindings: The trusted RAF command runs synchronously as a child of the Codex PreToolUse hook, which previously omitted timeout. Codex's default hook timeout is independent of the configured test-run execution deadline and includes admission waiting.

On command-hook timeout Codex terminates the hook process group, including its waiting RAF wrapper, then proceeds with the original native tool input. This explains a mechanism for both owner loss and the subsequent sandbox reader-lease write failure.

prepareCodexRafCommandAccess previously returned the original sandbox invocation when app-server hook protocol was unavailable. It also accepted an inspected definition without checking effective timeoutSec or async delivery.

externalContractSources.supports: Default PreToolUse timeout and fail-open behavior on hook errors/timeouts.
The timeout covers waiting for hook process output; dropping the process-tree guard terminates the Unix process group.

regressions.name: queued admission
regressions.method: Read the unchanged effective definition through installed Codex hooks/list. Spawn the actual generated hook and a gated wrapper fixture. Advance the external lifecycle contract's clock beyond two configured unit execution budgets; when the effective hook deadline has expired, apply its process-group kill. Assert owner survival, exact stdout/stderr/code delivery through result replay, and one wrapper invocation. Virtual time avoids a ten-minute unit test.

regressions.name: missing hook protocol
regressions.method: An executable which emits invalid app-server protocol while keeping stdin open must cause prepare rejection, rather than returning an invocation which can execute the original RAF command in the sandbox.

regressions.name: unsafe effective deadline
regressions.method: An initialized app-server which exposes the exact hook command but reports a short effective timeout must cause prepare rejection.

regressions.name: native timeout control
regressions.method: Real installed Codex, an isolated local scripted HTTP provider, and the production hook command with a deliberate one-second external hook timeout. Verify actual original-wrapper death and actual original-command sandbox fallback write refusal. The compressed deadline is a fixture control, not production configuration or a change to the unit execution policy.

appliedFix.hookTimeout: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER seconds is a protocol representation of no independent transport budget; it is not a unit, integration, admission, or cleanup policy. The wrapper continues to own execution deadline and cleanup from conf. Main explicitly confirmed this interpretation in this session.
appliedFix.inspection: Require the effective hook lifetime and synchronous delivery before trusting the inspected definition.
appliedFix.unavailable: Refuse launch when the trusted hook protocol is unavailable.

nativeControlResult: Passed in fd867c19 and 0ebab2fc: installed Codex actually killed the waiting owner and attempted the original command in its native sandbox, where the activation-lock fixture write was refused.
fixtureCorrections: Initial native control permitted writes to /tmp and therefore reproduced fallback without the expected EROFS. The corrected control excludes both TMPDIR and /tmp from native sandbox writes.
Initial no-protocol executable exited immediately and could race stdin writes with EPIPE. The corrected fixture emits invalid protocol and keeps stdin open.
deliveryLimit: Existing already-launched sessions retain their immutable hook definition. Main must deploy/activate the committed fix for new launches; this executor did not activate or push.
